item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload API, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, retains FilesOption, and verifies replayed multipart content. Candidate B changes the required API and introduces explicitly prohibited option and retry machinery.","reasons":["A implements the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). B instead exposes ...AddFileOption, breaking the frozen API contract and existing FilesOption behavior.","A directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), producing the required replayable multipart body with the correct field and filename.","A’s retry test parses both attempts and verifies multipart field name, uploaded filename, and content, giving strong evidence that streamed content is replayed intact after a 429.","B adds association fields and a parallel AddFileOption system despite the explicit prohibition on association fields and duplicate option machinery. It also duplicates Add’s request/response logic instead of routing through Add and preserving one implementation path shared with it and instead performs a broad RawClient retry refactor despite the contract explicitly ruling that out. Its makeBodyReplayable silently ignores io.ReadAll errors after potentially consuming part of the request body, which weakens source-reader error semantics globally."],"risks_a":["Upload calls the extracted private add helper rather than FilesService.Add itself, so it does not literally satisfy the requirement to route through the existing Add method.","A changes Add to eagerly buffer every custom body, contrary to the instruction to preserve Add’s existing behavior; this changes read timing and memory use.","The added tests do not cover empty-filename validation, nil content, or source-reader failures as required."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong public option type and therefore fails the exact required API contract.","It adds prohibited association options and expands multipartbody with unnecessary field support.","It duplicates FilesService.Add request construction, option handling, decoding, and errors rather than delegating to Add. It also refactors retry behavior for every raw request, well beyond task scope, with silently swallowed body-read failures and potential partial-body corruption. The tests do not demonstrate Upload retry behavior or source-reader error propagation."]}
